basics.name: Tushar Nayak
basics.label: Scientist, SurgBioMech / Pocivavsek Lab
basics.summary: Scientist at the University of Chicago working at the intersection of surgical biomechanics, computer vision, and medical imaging.

work.name: University of Chicago, SurgBioMech / Pocivavsek Lab
work.summary: Researching surgical biomechanics, computer vision, and medical imaging with a focus on geometry-aware methods for clinical data.
highlights: Developing vision systems for image-guided intervention and deformable surgical scenes.
Building methods that connect sparse clinical measurements to anatomy, motion, and deformation estimates.

work.name: Carnegie Mellon University
work.position: Graduate Student Researcher, Computational Engineering and Robotics Lab
work.summary: Master's thesis research on computer vision for image-guided robotic intervention and endovascular tele-surgery.
highlights: Built a pipeline for synthetic vessel deformation data generation, multi-view X-ray rendering, and physics auditing for endovascular intervention research.
Developed MorphPINN, a multimodal network that fuses fluoroscopy with 3D geometric context to predict vessel deformation from sparse imaging.
Contributed the vision subsystem section to a literature review on robot-assisted endovascular surgery currently under review at the Journal of Intelligent and Robotic Systems.

work.name: University of Pittsburgh, Surreality Lab
work.summary: Researching real-time registration and 3D reconstruction for medical imaging data with collaborators across robotic surgery projects.
highlights: Working with Rishi Basdeo under Professors Edward Andrews and Jacob Biehl.
Extending master's thesis work toward clinical mixed-reality and surgical visualization settings.

work.name: Carnegie Mellon University
work.position: Graduate Research Assistant, Glioblastoma Evolution Prediction
work.summary: Developed longitudinal MRI forecasting models for glioblastoma progression using Neural ODE-based approaches.
highlights: Built attention U-Net plus Neural ODE forecasting pipelines for multimodal MRI using FLAIR, T1, T2, and post-contrast T1 data.
Compared multiple model branches, including prefix-history forecasting and physics-informed variants, against persistence baselines.
Presented the work at Carnegie Mellon's 2025 Biomedical Engineering research forum.

work.name: Carnegie Mellon University
work.summary: Course support across graduate classes in deep learning, computer vision, and biomedical engineering.
highlights: Applied Deep Learning, Spring 2025, with Dr. Clarence Worrell.
Fundamentals of Computational Biomedical Engineering, Fall 2025, with Dr. Jason Szafron.
Computer Vision for Engineers, Fall 2025, with Dr. Kenji Shimada.
Machine Learning in Experimental Biomedical Engineering Research, Spring 2026, with Dr. Newell Washburn.

projects.name: Physics-Informed Endovasculature Deformation Estimation and Registration
projects.summary: Master's thesis project on modeling vessel deformation from fluoroscopy for image-guided endovascular robotics.
highlights: Synthetic vessel deformation generation with free-form deformation and guidewire kinematics.
Multi-view X-ray rendering across clinically relevant projections.
Multimodal deformation prediction with geometry-aware learning.

projects.name: Spatiotemporal Glioblastoma Evolution Visual Prediction
projects.summary: Neural ODE-based forecasting of future glioblastoma appearance from longitudinal multimodal MRI.
highlights: Attention U-Net plus Neural ODE modeling.
History-conditioned forecasting across MRI timepoints.
Evaluation against simple persistence baselines.

projects.name: Open Horizon Robotics Perception Curriculum
projects.summary: Open-source computer vision curriculum spanning classical vision, deep learning, 3D vision, geometry, and perception physics.
highlights: Authoring learning material for perception and prerequisite mathematics.
Mentoring student-led projects in the Open Horizon Robotics community.
